mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic demand, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher when GDP increases (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment above 4% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns remain positive when unemployment exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment and employment suggest labor market contradictions, leading to positive S&P returns.
failure_condition: Returns are not positive when both proxies increase.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate in a tightening cycle leads to negative S&P returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are positive when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production boosts S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns do not increase with rising production.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation above 310 leads to negative S&P returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: Returns remain positive when CPI exceeds 310.

mechanism_narrative: Both GDP and retail sales increasing indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are not positive when both proxies increase.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery, rising housing starts boost S&P returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns do not increase with rising housing starts.
